text: 诺贝尔奖得主、经济学家保罗·克鲁格曼表示，法国正面临潜在债务危机，对欧洲央行而言可能已经“大到救不了”。 法国学生因教育经费不足持续抗议，总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔尼则在努力推动一份充满争议的2027年预算案，该预算案试图实施数百亿美元的财政紧缩。 克鲁格曼周四在其Substack博客文章中写道，法国正走在“财政不可持续”的道路上，政府债务利息负担不断加重，而庞大的预算赤字又进一步推高了债务占GDP的比例。
text_en: Nobel laureate and economist Paul Krugman said France is facing a potential debt crisis and may already be "too big to save" for the European Central Bank. French students have continued protesting over insufficient education funding, while Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu is striving to push through a controversial 2027 budget that seeks to implement tens of billions of dollars in fiscal austerity. Krugman wrote in his Substack blog on Thursday that France is on a path of "fiscal unsustainability," with the interest burden on government debt steadily increasing, while a massive budget deficit further pushes up the debt-to-GDP ratio.
